in_english.name: Jephthah
in_english.long_meaning: Jephthah is a biblical name derived from Hebrew roots, meaning God opens his way, and refers to the judge of Israel in the Old Testament, who led the Israelites to victory against the Ammonites and is known for his faith and obedience to God

data.cultural_impact: Jephthah was a legendary Israelite warrior and leader, who is best known for leading the Israelites to victory against the Ammonites during a time when the Israelites were experiencing division and chaos. His name, meaning "God has judged," reflected his role as a deliverer and judge of his people. Jephthah's story is found in the book of Judges in the Old Testament of the Bible.
data.spiritual_significance: Jephthah's name also holds great spiritual significance as it emphasizes God's active role in the lives of His people. The name affirms the belief that God raises up leaders and delivers His people from their enemies. It is a reminder of God's faithfulness and provision, even in the midst of difficult times. Additionally, Jephthah's story shows the importance of humility and repentance, as he was originally rejected by his own people but later welcomed back through God's intervention.
data.spiritual_symbolism: A judge of Israel, Jephthah vowed to sacrifice the first thing that came out of his house upon his return victorious from battle. Upon his triumphant return, his daughter came out to greet him, and he kept his vow, leading to deep regret. His name may symbolize the inescapable consequences of hasty promises.

biblical_reference.note: Jephthah is a major figure in the book of Judges, known for his military victories and his vow to sacrifice his daughter to God

historical_references.reference: Jephthah was the son of Gilead, a mighty man of valor, who rescued the Gileadites from the Ammonites.
Jephthah vowed to the Lord that if He gave him victory over the Ammonites, he would offer as a burnt offering the first person who came out of his house to greet him upon his return.

platforms: Literature, particularly in retellings of the Bible story
Art, particularly in religious art depicting the story of Jephthah
Theater, particularly in productions of biblical plays
modern_usage.modern_context: Jephthah is a well-known figure in Jewish and Christian history, often remembered for his controversial vow to sacrifice the first person he saw upon his return from battle if he was victorious. While the historical accuracy of Jephthah's story is debated, it has been retold and reimagined in various forms of literature, art, and theater. Jephthah's story is particularly popular in religious education and is used to teach lessons about the importance of keeping promises and the consequences of rash vows.

name_in_real_life.story: Sarah Jephthah, a minister in Rome, Italy, shares that their name Jephthah meaning "God has judged" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
